t2049.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Zuhayr ibn Muhammad al-Tamimi, Abu al-Mundhir al-Khurasani, who lived in Syria then the Hijaz: the transmission of the Syrians from him is not sound, so he was weakened; al-Bukhari quotes Ahmad saying the Zuhayr the Syrians transmit from seems another person, and Abu Hatim said he narrated in Syria from memory and erred much; of the seventh generation, he died in 262.
as: رواية أهل الشام عنه غير مستقيمة فضعف بسببها
The transmission of the people of Syria from him is not sound, so he was weakened because of it
كأن زهيرا الذي يروي عنه الشاميون آخر
It is as if the Zuhayr from whom the Syrians transmit is another person
حدث بالشام من حفظه فكثر غلطه
He narrated in Syria from his memory, so his errors became many

as: Truthful but extremely bad in memory
Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Qaṭṭān, quoted by al-Mizzī
كان يحيى بن سعيد يضعف ابن أبي ليلى.
Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd considered Ibn Abī Laylā weak.
Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, quoted by al-Mizzī
كان سئ الحفظ، مضطرب الحديث، كان فقه ابن أبي ليلى أحب إلينا من حديثه، في حديثه اضطراب
He had poor memory and transmitted inconsistently. We prefer his jurisprudence to his hadith, which contains inconsistencies.
Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn, quoted by al-Mizzī
He is not up to standard.
ما رأيت أحدا أسوأ حفظا من ابن أبي ليلى.
I never saw anyone with worse memory than Ibn Abī Laylā.
أفادني ابن أبي ليلى أحاديث فإذا هي مقلوبة
Ibn Abī Laylā gave me hadiths, and they turned out to be garbled.
He was the most knowledgeable jurist in the world.
كان فقيها صاحب سنة، صدوقا، جائز الحديث.
He was a jurist who followed the Sunna, truthful and acceptable in hadith.
Abū Zurʿah al-Rāzī, quoted by al-Mizzī
Abū Ḥātim al-Rāzī, quoted by al-Mizzī
محله الصدق، كان سئ الحفظ، شغل بالقضاء فساء حفظه، لايتهم بشيء من الكذب إنما ينكر عليه كثرة الخطأ، يكتب حديثه ولا يحتج به
His standing is truthfulness; he had a poor memory, worsened by his judgeship; not accused of lying, only faulted for many errors; his hadith is written but not used as proof.
Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, quoted by al-Mizzī
ابن أبي ليلى ضعيف، وفي عطاء أكثر خطأ
Ibn Abī Laylā is weak, and errs most in (narrations from) ʿAṭāʾ.
أحمد بن يونس, quoted by al-Mizzī
كان زائدة لا يروي عن ابن أبي ليلى، وكان قد ترك حديثه
Zāʾidah did not narrate from Ibn Abī Laylā and had abandoned his hadith.
In our estimation, he is the most knowledgeable of people.
أنا تعلمنا جودة القراءة عند ابن أبي ليلى
We learned to recite well under Ibn Abī Laylā.

t6188.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAlqama ibn Waqqāṣ al-Laythī al-Madanī as truthful but having illusions, of the sixth generation, who died in 45 according to the correct view.
as: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Qaṭṭān, quoted by al-Mizzī
Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr ranks above Suhayl ibn Abī Ṣāliḥ.
Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Qaṭṭān, quoted by al-Mizzī
ليس هو ممن تريد، وكان يقول: حدثنا أشياخنا أبو سلمة، ويحيى ين عبد الرحمن بن حاطب
Under strict scrutiny he is not the one you seek. He used to say, ‘Our teachers Abū Salamah and Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ḥāṭib told us.’
Mālik gave a judgment similar to the one Yaḥyā had given.
وأما محمد ابن عمرو فرجل صالح ليس بأحفظ الناس للحديث
Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr was an upright man with less than the strongest memory for hadith.
Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn, quoted by al-Mizzī
ما زال الناس يتقون حديثه. قيل له، وما علة ذلك؟ قال: كان يحدث مرة عن أبي سلمة بالشئ من رأيه ثم يحدث به مرة أخرى عن أبي سلمة عن أبي هريرة
People had long been cautious about his hadith. He would give something first as Abū Salamah’s opinion, then transmit it through Abū Salamah from Abū Hurayrah.
Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn, quoted by al-Mizzī
أيهما يقدم؟ فقال: محمد ابن عمرو
Ibn Maʿīn preferred Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr to Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq.
إبراهيم بن يعقوب السعدي الجوزجاني, quoted by al-Mizzī
He is not strong in hadith, though his reports are sought.
Abū Ḥātim al-Rāzī, quoted by al-Mizzī
صالح الحديث، يكتب حديثه، وهو شيخ
His hadith is acceptable and should be recorded. He is a shaykh.
ليس به بأس. وقال في موضع آخر: ثقة
There is no objection to him. Elsewhere al-Nasāʾī called him reliable.
له حديث صالح، وقد حدث عنه جماعة من الثقات كل واحد منهم ينفرد عنه بنسخة، ويغرب بعضهم على بعض، ويروي عنه مالك غير حديث في "الموطأ "، وأرجو أنه لا بأس به

He has acceptable hadith. Several reliable transmitters each transmit a distinct collection from him and give reports unknown to the others. Mālik transmits several of his reports in the Muwaṭṭaʾ. I hope there is no objection to him.
وذكره ابن حبان في كتاب "الثقات" ، وقال: كان يخطئ
Ibn Ḥibbān listed him among reliable transmitters and said he made mistakes.
Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Qaṭṭān, quoted by al-Mizzī
محمد بن عمرو أحب إلي من ابن أبي حرملة
I prefer Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr to Ibn Abī Ḥarmalah.
He transmitted many hadith and was considered weak.

t7785.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Yazīd ibn Abī Nashbah al-Sulamī as unknown (majhūl) and belonging to the fifth generation. He is among the teachers of Abū Dāwūd.

t7819.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Yaʿqūb ibn Abī Salamah al-Mājishūn al-Taymī, Abū Yūsuf al-Madanī, as truthful, of the fourth generation, who died after 120.

t782.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Bilāl ibn Kaʿb al-ʿAkī as acceptable (maqbūl), of the seventh generation.

t8061.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Abū Ḥakīm, father of Ismāʿīl, said to be a client of ʿUthmān, as unknown, of the third generation.

t8128.bio: Ibn Ḥajar describes Abū Saʿīd al-Ḥimyarī, a Syrian, as unknown, of the third generation, and his report from Muʿādh ibn Jabal as mursal.

t8195.bio: Ibn Ḥajar gives Abū ʿĀṣim al-ʿIbādānī al-Baṣrī's name as ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUbayd Allāh or the reverse, alternatively Ibn ʿAbd without idāfah, calling him weak in hadith and of the eighth generation.
as: Weak in hadith, of the eighth generation.

t8230.bio: Ibn Ḥajar describes Abū ʿUbayda ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Zamʿa al-Qurashī al-Asadī as acceptable (maqbūl) and of the third generation. Muslim, Abū Dāwūd, al-Nasāʾī, and Ibn Mājah cite him.
as: He is acceptable (i.e., his reports are accepted when corroborated).

t8384.bio: Ibn Ḥajar lists Abū Maʿn Muḥammad ibn Maʿn, who transmits from Zahra ibn Maʿbad and from whom Ibn al-Mubārak transmits, as acceptable and of the seventh generation; it is said Nisāʾī transmitted from him.

t8403.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Abū Mūsā, a teacher of Muʿāwiya ibn Ṣāliḥ, as unknown, of the sixth generation.

t8476.bio: Ibn Ḥajar states his name is Yazīd.

t8678.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Laylā bint Qānif al-Thaqafiyyah as a female Companion who has a hadith.

t913.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Jarīr ibn Zayd al-Azdī, Abū Salamah, paternal uncle of Jarīr ibn Ḥāzim, as ṣadūq, of the sixth generation.

t966.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Jumayʿ ibn ʿUmayr al-ʿIjlī, Abū Bakr al-Kūfī, as weak and a Rāfiḍī, of the eighth generation.
